Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings  
• Immediate onset of shallow breathing, chest tightness, tingling lips, and blotchy skin rash within minutes of wasp sting.  
• No previous similar reactions; has antihistamine available but not yet taken.  

Working diagnosis  
• Suspected early anaphylaxis secondary to wasp sting—high likelihood given rapid multisystem involvement (respiratory + cutaneous).  

Differential considerations (consistent with DDx)  
• Systemic allergic urticaria without full anaphylaxis – monitor for progression.  
• Anxiety/panic-induced hyperventilation – low likelihood given objective rash and allergen trigger.  

Management provided  
• Advised immediate ambulance activation (wife calling 999).  
• Instructed to take oral antihistamine while awaiting paramedics.  
• Urgent ED assessment for potential epinephrine administration and observation recommended.

1. Anaphylaxis secondary to wasp sting – High likelihood: temporal relationship, respiratory compromise, and cutaneous signs.  
2. Systemic allergic urticaria (without anaphylaxis) – Medium likelihood: rash and lip tingling present, but respiratory symptoms raise concern for escalation.
